title: Boston Red Sox Announce Major Adley Rutschman News Before Blue Jays Series
description: The Boston Red Sox announced major news on trade acquisition Adley Rutschman before the Toronto Blue Jays series. The post Boston Red Sox Announce Major Adley Rutschman News Before Blue Jays Series appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Boston Red Sox are slated to begin a four-game series against the Toronto Blue Jays at Rogers Centre in Toronto on Monday.

Ahead of the series, the Boston Red Sox revealed major Adley Rutschman news to reporters.

GettyHOUSTON, TEXAS – JULY 18: Adley Rutschman #35 of the Baltimore Orioles runs to first base during the fifth inning against the Houston Astros at Daikin Park on July 18, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Alex Slitz/Getty Images)

MassLive's Christopher Smith wrote (X): "Adley Rutschman is traveling with the Red Sox to Toronto but there won't be a roster move Monday. He'll have a workout day at Rogers Centre, then they will decide when to activate him."

MLB.com's Ian Browne wrote (X): "Adley Rutschman will fly to Toronto with the Red Sox tonight, work out with the team tomorrow and could be active as soon as Tuesday."

GettyHOUSTON, TEXAS – JULY 17: Adley Rutschman #35 of the Baltimore Orioles runs after hitting a double during the eighth inning against the Houston Astros at Daikin Park on July 17, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Alex Slitz/Getty Images)

The Red Sox acquired Rutschman and catcher Jake Rogers from the Baltimore Orioles in exchange for right-handed pitching prospect Anthony Eyanson, catcher Carlos Narváez, right-hander Kyson Witherspoon, outfielder Endyy Azocar and a player to be named later.

Eyanson is MLB Pipeline's No. 49 overall prospect. Witherspoon ranked as the Red Sox's No. 4 overall prospect, and Azocar ranked as the organization's No. 5.

GettyPHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA – JULY 14: Adley Rutschman #35 of the Baltimore Orioles grounds out to the shortstop during the eighth inning of the 2026 MLB All-Star Game at Citizens Bank Park on July 14, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images)

Rutschman has been on the injured list since July 20 with left wrist inflammation. He just completed a two-game rehab assignment with Boston's Triple-A affiliate. The catcher went 1-for-5 with a double, two RBI and two walks during the rehab stint.

Rutschman, the 2019 first overall pick, is a three-time All-Star and former Silver Slugger. He has posted 16.7 bWAR and a .254/.342/.414 slash line with 69 home runs and 277 RBI in five big-league seasons, all with Baltimore.

title: Why NHL Forward Noah Philp Walked Away From Hockey at Just 27 Years Old
description: A promising center retires weeks after signing a new contract, revealing a deeper struggle few saw coming.
fullText:
Professional hockey has lost a player whose journey was anything but conventional. Just weeks after putting pen to paper on a deal with Swedish Hockey League club HV71, a 27-year-old forward shocked the hockey world by announcing his permanent retirement from the sport. The timing caught many off guard, but the signs had been there for years.

Noah Philp was never selected in the NHL Draft, yet he managed to carve out a path to the highest level of the sport through sheer determination and skill. After lighting up the WHL as a prolific scorer with the Seattle Thunderbirds, Philp attended the University of Alberta before turning professional in the spring of 2022 with the Edmonton Oilers organization. His rookie campaign with the Bakersfield Condors in the AHL during the 2022-2023 season was impressive, tallying 37 points across 70 games and establishing himself as a genuine development success story.

However, it was precisely at that juncture that Philp's trajectory took an unexpected turn. Instead of building on his momentum and pushing for a full-time NHL roster spot, the 6-foot-3 center stepped away from the game entirely for a full season. That initial departure hinted that thoughts of retirement were already swirling in his mind far earlier than they do for most professional athletes.

When he returned for the 2024-2025 campaign, Philp picked up right where he left off, posting 35 points in 55 AHL contests and earning his first NHL call-up. He appeared in 15 games with the Oilers. The following season, he earned a spot on Edmonton's roster out of training camp but managed only three points in 15 games before being placed on waivers in early December. The Carolina Hurricanes claimed him off the wire, though his time in Carolina at the NHL level was fleeting, consisting of just two games. He spent the remainder of the season in the AHL with the Chicago Wolves, where he was outstanding during the playoffs, recording 14 points in 21 postseason games as the team advanced all the way to the Calder Cup Final.

In a statement released through HV71, Philp apologized to the Swedish club for the awkward timing of his announcement. He had only recently signed a one-year contract that included an option for a second season. Despite the unfortunate circumstances, Philp chose transparency over pretense, explaining that his motivation for hockey was no longer fully there. Rather than go through the motions and fail to give his all on the ice, he felt it was more respectful to be upfront about where he stood mentally.

HV71 acknowledged the situation and confirmed they would move quickly to find a replacement to fill the gap in their lineup. The club's measured response underscored a mutual respect between player and organization, even in a difficult moment.

Philp's retirement closes the book on a career that, while relatively brief, was genuinely inspiring in its arc from undrafted college player to NHL regular. His story serves as a powerful reminder that talent and opportunity alone do not sustain a career at the professional level. The human element, particularly internal drive and personal fulfillment, plays an equally critical role. For Philp, stepping away was not a sign of weakness but an act of self-awareness that few athletes are willing to embrace so openly.

title: The Giants are signing another defensive back
description: J.T. Woods tried out last week, and visited the Giants on Sunday.
fullText:
The New York Giants, a bit thin in their secondary with nickel cornerback Dru Phillips ailing and cornerback Jarrick Bernard-Converse having been waived, are adding help at that spot.

Per Aaron Wilson, the Giants are signing Pdefensive back J.T. Woods. Woods visited the team on Sunday. Woods was part of an eight-player workout held by the Giants on Tuesday in West Virginia. Defensive backs David Long and D.J. James, along with offensive lineman Brandon Jaimes, have also been signed by the team after that workout.

A third-round pick by the Los Angeles Chargers in 2022, Woods played in 13 games for the Chargers over two seasons. He has not played in an NFL game the past two seasons. During that time, he has been on the practice squads of the Philadelphia Eagles, Chicago Bears, Seattle Seahawks, Las Vegas Raiders, and New York Jets.

The Giants return to practice on Monday at the Quest Diagnostics Training Center in East Rutherford, N.J.

title: Can Oklahoma Make The College Football Playoff With A 9-3 Record? Paul Finebaum Thinks So...
description: The ESPN host claims the Sooners' brutal SEC gauntlet offers a rare lifeline, potentially rewarding a three-loss campaign with an unprecedented invitation to the expanded postseason
fullText:
Paul Finebaum isn't usually one to hand out easy paths, but he recently put Oklahoma in a small group of teams that could still reach the College Football Playoff even with three losses.

Speaking on The Paul Finebaum Show on ESPN Radio and the SEC Network, he laid it out clearly. "There are a couple of teams that would have a really good shot at making it at 9-3," Finebaum said. "Texas would be one. Oklahoma would be another. To get in with three losses, you better have played a significant schedule and nonconference. I think those are the two. LSU, probably because of playing Clemson."

Finebaum is acknowledging both the strength of Oklahoma's schedule and the reality of how the expanded playoff works. A tough slate can create a path that softer schedules simply don't have.

Still, history shows how difficult that path actually is.

No 9-3 team has ever made the College Football Playoff.

Two teams have gotten in at 10-3 — Clemson in 2024 and Alabama in 2025 — but both played in their conference championship games. That extra data point matters. A 9-3 team only plays 12 games and doesn't get the benefit of a 13th against another strong opponent in a title game.

Recent near-misses drive the point home. In 2024, Alabama sat at 9-3 and was the first team left out when 11-2 SMU got in. In 2025, Texas finished 9-3 and was the third team on the outside looking in. Those examples show that while the door isn't completely closed, it's a very narrow one.

The current playoff format makes it even tougher, with the new rules in place this season. Now, all four Power conference champions receive automatic bids, and Notre Dame gets an automatic berth if it finishes in the top 12 of the final CFP rankings. That setup locks in several spots and leaves fewer at-large opportunities for three-loss teams, no matter how impressive their résumés look on paper.

Finebaum isn't wrong that Oklahoma's schedule gives it a better shot than most. Games against Michigan, Georgia, Texas and the rest of a brutal SEC gauntlet create the kind of résumé strength the committee has historically rewarded. A couple of those wins, especially on the road or against ranked teams, would carry significant weight. But relying on a 9-3 finish still feels like playing with fire.

The more realistic and healthier goal for this team is 10-2 or better. A 10-2 record with Oklahoma's schedule would essentially lock up a playoff spot. That should be the standard.

The pieces are there for it — a healthy John Mateer, a loaded defense, and more experience across the roster than Brent Venables has had in previous seasons. The early stretch with Michigan, Georgia and Texas will go a long way toward deciding whether that 10-win threshold is reachable.

Finebaum's comment is fair in the sense that the door isn't completely shut at 9-3 for a team with this kind of schedule.

It's just a door that almost never opens.

Oklahoma is better off treating three losses as a worst-case scenario rather than a viable backup plan. Win the games they're supposed to win, take care of business in the middle of the league slate, and put themselves in position where the committee doesn't have to debate them.

The Sooners have already shown they can compete at a high level in the SEC. Last year's playoff appearance proved that. The next step is consistency and finishing with a record that removes any doubt.

Finebaum giving them a path at 9-3 is interesting. Making sure they don't need that path is the better approach.

title: Nick Suzuki Ranked Above Auston Matthews in New NHL Center Rankings
description: A new ranking places the Canadiens captain ahead of Toronto's star in a surprising shakeup.
fullText:
The 2025-26 season proved to be a defining chapter in the career of Nick Suzuki. Montreal's captain reached milestones that only a select few players ever achieve, and the hockey world is finally starting to give him the credit he deserves. A recently released ranking from The Hockey News has now put an official stamp on what many fans in Montreal have believed for some time.

Suzuki posted 29 goals and 101 points during the 2025-26 campaign, crossing the coveted 100-point threshold and firmly establishing himself among the NHL's elite playmakers. On top of that offensive explosion, he took home the Selke Trophy as the league's best defensive forward, a recognition that speaks volumes about his two-way game and his commitment to every aspect of hockey.

The 14th jersey in Montreal carried enormous weight this past season. Suzuki served as the anchor of the top line for what was the second-youngest roster in the entire NHL. Despite the team's youth, his leadership helped guide the Canadiens all the way to the Eastern Conference Finals, a remarkable achievement for a franchise still in its rebuilding phase.

When The Hockey News compiled its list of the top three centers in the Atlantic Division, Suzuki landed at number two. The only player ranked above him was Florida Panthers star Aleksander Barkov. While the Finnish center has never reached the 100-point mark in a single season, his resume featuring two Stanley Cup championships and three Selke Trophies gives him an edge that is hard to argue against.

Perhaps the most striking takeaway from the ranking is the placement of Auston Matthews. The Toronto Maple Leafs captain, long considered one of the most dangerous offensive weapons in the sport, was slotted behind Suzuki at third in the division. His last two seasons have fallen well short of the standards he set earlier in his career, and that decline carried significant weight in the evaluation.

At his peak, Matthews likely still surpasses Suzuki in terms of pure offensive firepower. However, it has been quite some time since the Leafs star performed at the level he displayed in 2023-24, when he lit the lamp 69 times and finished third in Selke Trophy voting.

For Suzuki, this ranking represents something larger than a spot on a list. It signals a shift in perception across the league. He is no longer viewed simply as a promising player on a rebuilding team but rather as one of the premier centers in all of professional hockey. With the Canadiens' young core continuing to develop around him, the trajectory suggests even bigger things could be on the horizon for Montreal's captain.

title: New Michigan basketball coach Mike Boynton is married to former West Ottawa star athlete Jenny Hill
description: Don't be surprised if you see Michigan's new head basketball coach around West Michigan. His wife is from Holland and was a star athlete at WO.
fullText:
GRAND RAPIDS - Jenny Boynton was at her parents' house in Holland last month when she got some big news.

Her husband, Mike Boynton Jr., was just named head coach of the University of Michigan basketball team.

"I love it," she said. "We joked when this became a possibility … I started wearing blue around the house to hint that this is where we needed to be.'"

Boynton - whose maiden name is Jenny Hill - graduated from West Ottawa High School in 2000. She played volleyball and basketball for the Panthers. She would go on to play volleyball at Virginia Tech.

"Just through college athletics," Mike Boynton said. "She was a dietician and I was the head assistant coach at the University of South Carolina back in 2008."

Mike Boynton would eventually become head coach at Oklahoma State University for seven years before taking a job as assistant coach at Michigan last year under Dusty May. The Wolverines won the National Championship and May left to coach in the NBA. So that left the door open for Boynton.

The Boyntons were Grand Rapids on Sunday to watch their son, Ace, play basketball at the Bank Hoops Underclassman All-State Camp. Ace will be an eighth grader this fall.

"I've been to Grand Rapids several times," he said. "My wife is from Holland. We fly into Grand Rapids to see her parents (Brian and Nancy Hill)."

One of Jenny Boynton's good friends is Kristen Redell, the wife of West Ottawa basketball coach Jared Redell. They were all at West Ottawa around the same time.

"I was a few years behind guys like (football player) Rob Renes and (basketball player) Jared Redell," she said. "They were a few years older than me, but they were big names when I was there."

One of the first people she called when she got the news was Kristen Redell. The two were teammates on the volleyball team at West Ottawa.

"Jenny was at her parents house in Holland when they found out that Mike got the job," Redell said. "When they came to Holland recently, we got them into the gym at West Ottawa so the boys could get shots up. Our sons are the same age."

Redell said she her family has always been fans of Michigan basketball.

"Its amazing," she said. "We love Michigan (basketball). We were excited that Mike got the position. It is an amazing tie to West Michigan and the Holland community."

The Boyton's will be back in West Michigan in October. The University of Michigan will play an exhibition on Oct. 25 against the University of Houston at Van Andel Arena.

title: Packers claim former HS All-American receiver Chris Hilton
description: Chris Hilton was a combine invite in 2026 and participated in four pre-draft all-star games
fullText:
The Green Bay Packers worked out multiple receivers today and re-signed receiver Kisean Johnson after a tryout, following short-term injuries to receivers Matthew Golden and Jayden Reed. When the Packers announced their transactions after practice Sunday, which Johnson participated in, it was news that Green Bay waived two players, not one, while adding Johnson, giving the team an open roster spot on the 91-man roster. The players waived were cornerback Marlon Jones and safety Johnathan Baldwin, who both were given injury designations. They will revert to the Packers' injured reserve if they pass through waivers unclaimed. From there, Green Bay can decide whether to end their seasons by keeping them on the injured reserve or pay them out an injury settlement, which would make them free agents while they are rehabbing their injuries.

As I mentioned in The Feed when the news dropped that the Packers had an extra roster spot to fill, this seemed like a move that a team would make before they claimed someone on waivers themselves. It turns out that I was on the right path, as Green Bay was awarded another receiver, Chris Hilton Jr., off waivers today. He should make his Packers debut in Monday's practice, which is open to the public.

Hilton played five years at LSU before going undrafted in the 2026 class, despite participating in four different all-star games (Hula Bowl, American Bowl, East-West Shrine Bowl and Senior Bowl) and receiving a combine invite. At the combine this year, he measured in at 6'0"-flat and 188 pounds and recorded a 4.41-second 40-yard dash.

The former high school All-American had 41 receptions for 780 yards and six touchdowns in his SEC career, but only registered 10 receptions for 122 yards as a redshirt senior, as the Tigers struggled in the passing game after quarterback Garrett Nussmeier injured his abs, which severely limited his play. Nussmeier, who had some first-round hype coming into the 2025 season, wound up going undrafted and signing with the Kansas City Chiefs this spring.

Chris Hilton has okay size for a WR and good speed. Explsoveness is neither a strength nor a weakness, but at his size those poor agility drills are likely to show up when facing NFL cornerbacks. Some things to work with, but some concerns. pic.twitter.com/GZ69HsueAG

Hilton began his NFL career with the Washington Commanders, but he was let go yesterday, a day after the team signed receiver Stefon Diggs to a one-year, $12 million contract.

When Hilton signed with Washington, he received $15,000 in guarantees, which was equal to or more than 6 of the Packers' 11 initial UDFA signings this year:

TE RJ Maryland (waived with an injury designation)

CB Marlon Jones (waived with an injury designation)

Commanders signed Chris Hilton Jr from LSU. I coached him in the Hula Bowl. Kid can play! Nice pickup

Hilton was The Athletic's Dane Brugler's 50th-ranked receiver in the 2026 draft class and received a free agent grade from the draft analyst. Here's his blurb on Hilton:

Christopher "Chris" Hilton Jr. grew up north of Baton Rouge, La., with his parents (Chris Sr. and Cindy), who were both track athletes at Southern University. Hilton was a standout football and track star at Zachary High, where he won several state titles in sprints and jumps (personal best of 10.85 seconds in the 100-meter dash).

A four-star recruit, he was the top-ranked receiver in LSU's 2021 class (ahead of Malik Nabers and Brian Thomas Jr.). Multiple injuries sidetracked his early career, however, as he struggled to find a consistent role beyond being a deep threat.

Hilton looks like a sprinter with his slender, lean-muscled frame and uses his speed to stretch the field. A limited snap count hindered his ability to develop as a route runner, and he was also up and down with his hands — his success rate nosedived when defenders crowded his air space. He has limited return experience but played more on special teams in 2025.

For what it's worth, the injuries he suffered in his career were:

2021 (redshirt season after playing four games): torn meniscus

2022: missed 10 games with shoulder surgery and a torn meniscus in his other knee

2024: missed 7 games with a hairline fracture

In total, he started seven games for the Tigers over five years. His only return experience was as a kick returner during his true freshman and redshirt freshman seasons, when he returned two attempts for a total of 26 yards.

The Packers also reported worked out Devin Voisin, a UDFA who was second-team All-Sun Belt with South Alabama last year, so it's clear that the team was trying to add bodies to the receiver position this week. Voisin has yet to sign with an NFL team, despite being on the Senior Bowl roster this offseason. He was invited to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers' rookie minicamp and has also worked out with the Tennessee Titans and Denver Broncos in the last two weeks.

title: Scott Gomez Has Completely Erased Montreal From His Life
description: The former NHLer refuses all contact with anything related to the Canadiens. The story behind his silence is painful.
fullText:
Some stints in professional hockey end quietly, with a player simply moving on to the next chapter. Others leave wounds so deep that they reshape a person's relationship with an entire city. For Scott Gomez, his time with the Montreal Canadiens falls squarely into the latter category, and the extent of the damage has only recently come to light in striking detail.

Journalist Richard Labbé shared a revealing anecdote on BPM Sports that illustrates just how thoroughly Gomez has severed ties with everything connected to the Canadiens organization and the city of Montreal. Labbé recounted how he attempted to set up a Zoom interview with Gomez through the NHL Network. Initially, things seemed promising, and the interview was confirmed. But roughly an hour later, the call came back with a firm and final answer: it was not going to happen. Gomez does not discuss Montreal. He does not want to discuss Montreal. He will not entertain any request that has anything to do with the Quebec metropolis.

The roots of Gomez's total estrangement trace back to one of the most infamous scoring droughts in modern NHL history. The American forward went an entire year without finding the back of the net while wearing the Canadiens jersey. What began as a frustrating slump quickly spiraled into something far more damaging: a full-blown spectacle of public ridicule.

The internet seized on his struggles with merciless creativity. Fans launched so-called "Loto-Gomez" websites where people could wager on when he would finally score his next goal. Inside the Bell Centre, the atmosphere became even more humiliating. Every time Gomez touched the puck, the crowd would erupt in sarcastic applause. Fans stood up and cheered mockingly. Some supporters even showed up wearing sombreros in the stands, turning each game into a carnival of derision directed at a single player.

According to Labbé, this episode stands out as one of the rare instances in professional hockey where a player became a public laughingstock in real time, right on the ice surface where he was trying to do his job. The cruelty of that treatment, sustained over months, appears to have left an indelible mark on Gomez.

While many athletes eventually find a way to look back on difficult chapters with some distance or even humor, Gomez has clearly chosen a different path. The fact that years after leaving the organization he still refuses any conversation remotely connected to Montreal speaks to the depth of the psychological toll. For a player who had enjoyed a successful career that included a Stanley Cup and significant contracts, the Montreal chapter remains a wound he has no interest in reopening. Whether time will ever soften that stance remains to be seen, but for now, the name Montreal is entirely off limits in Scott Gomez's world.

title: Hagen Smith, Colson Montgomery Lead White Sox to Series Win Over Guardians
description: Hagen Smith delivered two scoreless innings in his MLB debut, while Colson Montgomery’s three-run homer lifted the White Sox to a crucial series win.
fullText:
It will be the division games that matter most for the Chicago White Sox down the stretch of the 2026 season. And after suffering another difficult-to-stomach sweep at the hands of the Boston Red Sox, the White Sox answered with a big weekend series win over the Cleveland Guardians.

It all came down to Sunday's rubber match, when Davis Martin took the ball and surrendered two runs in the first inning before being removed from the game following a rain delay that lasted more than two hours.

The early stages of the game did not set up well for Chicago. While the offense jumped on Joey Cantillo with three consecutive hits to start the game, the White Sox left two runners in scoring position with nobody out in the bottom of the first inning. They then immediately went into the rain delay trailing 2-1, knowing their starting pitcher would be done for the day after recording just three outs.

That was a big blow for a White Sox team with an already taxed bullpen, one that had been pushed to the limit Thursday night in Boston during a 13-inning defeat. But with a key off day coming Monday, manager Will Venable emptied the tank, and the White Sox relievers proved up to the task. That included left-handed pitcher Hagen Smith, the No. 2 prospect in the White Sox organization, who made his MLB debut Sunday.

Smith's debut was true to form. He recorded his first MLB strikeout on three pitches against Brayan Rocchio, the first batter he faced. He struck out the side in his first inning of work, even managing to punch out the notoriously stingy Steven Kwan.

Smith's second inning, however, was much tougher. He walked three batters to load the bases with two outs, then worked a full count against Rocchio before inducing a lineout to third baseman Miguel Vargas. Smith escaped the jam despite issuing four walks on the day, ultimately throwing two scoreless innings and earning the win in his first MLB appearance.

He got that win thanks to Colson Montgomery, who stepped up with two runners on and two outs in the bottom of the third inning and pummeled a Craig Yoho pitch 110.7 mph for his 26th home run of the year. That blast put the White Sox on top 5-2, a lead they held for the rest of the afternoon.

The Colson Montgomery haters are in SHAMBLES!#WhiteSox lead 5-2 on his 26th home run. pic.twitter.com/zz9rq3tqqt

It was an impressive display by the White Sox, who picked themselves up off the mat following a rough start to the game. Both the offense and the pitching staff did enough to secure the win.

"We all stayed pretty much locked in," Montgomery said of the rain delay during his postgame interview with Brooke Fletcher. "We treated it like a whole new ballgame, 0-0."

That win gives the White Sox their largest division lead of the season. It also put a new team in Chicago's rearview mirror. The White Sox now hold a 3.5 game lead in the AL Central, and it is the red-hot Detroit Tigers who sit in second place, with Cleveland and Minnesota both 4.0 games back.

The Tigers are 7-2 over their last nine games. It's an ironic time for a hot streak after they traded both Tarik Skubal and Casey Mize at the MLB trade deadline, but they are by no means out of the race. The White Sox will have to keep taking care of business and stacking series wins if they want to run away with the AL Central crown.

A series win over the Guardians was a good start, but the difficult tests are not over. Next weekend, the White Sox will travel to Detroit for a three-game series against the Tigers.

title: Former Eagles draft pick returns for free-agent tryout
description: The Eagles hosted David Blay, Ja’Quinden Jackson and former draft pick Tarron Jackson as they evaluate depth at three positions
fullText:
The Philadelphia Eagles aren't waiting until the preseason opener to evaluate potential roster additions. According to the NFL transaction wire, Philadelphia hosted defensive tackle David Blay, running back Ja'Quinden Jackson, and linebacker Tarron Jackson for free-agent visits Sunday.

Workouts and visits don't guarantee a signing. Teams routinely evaluate available players during training camp to ensure they have up-to-date medical information and a list of potential replacements in case of injuries.

Still, Philadelphia's three visitors are worth examining. Blay is a local product coming off his final season at Miami. Ja'Quinden Jackson offers size and power at running back, while Tarron Jackson is a familiar face after beginning his NFL career with the Eagles.

Blay may be the most intriguing developmental prospect of the three. The Levittown, Pennsylvania, native signed with New England as an undrafted rookie after playing at West Chester, Louisiana Tech and Miami. The Patriots released him Friday, allowing Philadelphia to bring him in two days later. New England lists Blay at 6-foot-2 and 292 pounds. He played 46 games during his college career, finishing with 129 tackles, 11.5 sacks, one forced fumble and one pass breakup. He recorded 28 tackles during his final season at Miami. The Patriots signed him May 8 before releasing him Aug. 7.

Blay's most productive season came at Louisiana Tech in 2024. He recorded 46 tackles, 10.5 tackles for loss and 6.5 sacks while earning first-team All-Conference USA honors. Philadelphia already has Jalen Carter, Jordan Davis, Moro Ojomo and Byron Young occupying prominent places in the defensive tackle rotation. Gabe Hall is among the players competing for a reserve role. That makes Blay more of a developmental option than someone likely to earn immediate playing time.

His local ties, college production and recent availability make him a logical player to evaluate. Of the three visitors, Blay may have the clearest chance to receive a contract if the Eagles want another interior defender for the remainder of camp.

Jackson entered college as a quarterback before eventually moving to running back at Utah. His most productive season came after transferring to Arkansas. The 6-foot-2, 233-pound runner carried the ball 149 times for 790 yards and 15 touchdowns in 2024. He also caught 13 passes for 139 yards, displaying more receiving ability than his bruising frame might suggest.

Jackson signed with Jacksonville as an undrafted rookie in 2025. He carried 13 times for 56 yards and caught two passes for 13 yards during the preseason but didn't make the initial roster. He later returned to the Jaguars' practice squad and signed a reserve/futures deal before Jacksonville waived him May 11.

The Eagles already have Saquon Barkley leading a backfield that includes Tank Bigsby and Dameon Pierce. ShunDerrick Powell is also seeking a role. That makes an immediate signing less likely unless Philadelphia is dealing with an undisclosed injury or wants another runner to absorb preseason carries.

Jackson's power would give the Eagles another short-yardage option, but his path to the roster would be difficult.

Tarron Jackson requires little introduction inside the Jefferson Health Training Complex. Philadelphia selected him with the 191st overall pick in the sixth round of the 2021 NFL Draft. Jackson appeared in 21 games over his first two seasons with the Eagles. His lone NFL sack came against the Detroit Lions during his rookie year. title: Vollering wins Tour de France Femmes after war of nerves
description: Dutch rider Demi Vollering took the Tour de France Femmes overall title in style on Sunday, winning the hilly final stage to extend her lead on nearest rival Kasia Niewiadoma, who finished second overall after a tense struggle.The 29-year-old also won the 2023 title and earned her second one by timing the nine-day slog to perfection, carving out solo wins on the final two stages, which both ended in Nice.
fullText:
Dutch rider Demi Vollering took the Tour de France Femmes overall title in style on Sunday, winning the hilly final stage to extend her lead on nearest rival Kasia Niewiadoma, who finished second overall after a tense struggle.

The 29-year-old also won the 2023 title and earned her second one by timing the nine-day slog to perfection, carving out solo wins on the final two stages, which both ended in Nice.

"It's a dream to live this life," Vollering said after hoisting her bike above her head at the finish line.

"I knew my level and even when Kasia won on Mont Ventoux I was still confident," added Vollering, who has also finished second on this race three times in its five editions since being relaunched in 2022.

Vollering's FDJ-United Suez are the first French team to win the race, earning her high praise from team boss Stephen Delcourt.

"Through her high standards, sensitivity, authenticity, and the way she brings others along with her, she is redefining what it means to be a modern leader," he said.

"She inspires her teammates, she inspires the fans, she inspires an entire generation ... She doesn't just win races; she shows the way forward."

Vollering had to carve out this win.

Niewiadoma took the yellow jersey on Friday's climb of Mont Ventoux, setting up a pulsating finale.

Vollering then edged into the overall lead on Saturday, attacking late on a small hill and edging into an eight-second overall advantage over 2024 winner Niewiadoma.

A furious Niewiadoma, however, complained she had been blocked by a teammate of Vollering's at a crucial moment, but no action was taken.

Vollering said her team had been both "honest and humble" after Sunday's race, adding that her teammate Celia Gery, the alleged blocker, had received death threats on social media.

"Celia had a really bad night. I'm sure deep down that Kasia knows these kind of things can happen in a race," Vollering said.

The scene was set for a dramatic final stage contested over four climbs of the Col d'Eze just outside Nice, where Vollering waited until the fourth ascent to pounce.

Attacking near the summit, she took a 20sec lead and thundered down towards Nice, never looking back.

Italy's Elisa Longo Borghini came third overall after Swiss rider Marlen Reusser fell on a descent and lost a two-minute cushion on the podium.

Dutch sprinter Lorena Wiebes won the green sprint points jersey mainly thanks to her victories on the two opening stages in Switzerland.

Her compatriot Puck Pieterse secured the polka dot climb jersey ahead of the final stage.

The best young rider jersey was won by Germany's Antonia Niedermaier, who also finished fourth overall.

title: The NHL Salary Cap May Be Hiding a Massive Surprise Set to Reshape Hockey by 2028
description: Industry insiders agree: the NHL's official salary cap projections are far too low, and a seismic correction looms.
fullText:
Since the post-pandemic recovery, the NHL's salary cap has been climbing at a steady but modest pace. However, according to well-connected figures within the hockey industry, the real financial shakeup has yet to arrive. Executives, agents, and financial insiders are increasingly aligned on a striking observation: the league's publicly shared revenue figures do not accurately reflect the money actually flowing into the sport.

Reporting from James Mirtle of The Athletic paints a compelling picture. Every executive and player agent he spoke with over recent months reached the same conclusion: the salary cap projections the NHL has released through the 2027-2028 season are significantly lower than where revenues are actually trending. The gap between official estimates and observed financial performance has been widening since the pandemic, and it points to a substantial upward adjustment on the horizon.

This growing discrepancy suggests that a sharp increase in the salary cap could materialize as soon as the summer of 2028. Those closest to the league's financial machinery are unequivocal in their assessment: the numbers currently being published represent a floor, not a ceiling. The truly dramatic movement is still ahead.

Adding fuel to this trajectory is the prospect of new television broadcasting agreements. NHL viewership has remained strong, and a lucrative media rights deal would inject fresh revenue into the system. Such an influx could push the cap higher and faster than any current model anticipates, creating a financial environment that looks radically different from today's landscape.

The expectation of a significant cap increase is not just theoretical speculation. It is already shaping how teams and players approach contract talks. Players and their representatives are pushing harder at the bargaining table, emboldened by the belief that the financial pie is about to grow considerably. Meanwhile, organizations are showing a greater willingness to meet those demands, reasoning that contracts signed today at seemingly aggressive numbers will look like bargains within two or three years.

For general managers, the strategic calculus is shifting in profound ways. Long-term commitments that appear bold relative to the current cap could turn out to be shrewd investments if the upper limit rises as dramatically as insiders expect. Teams that position themselves with available cap space in the near future may find themselves holding a significant competitive advantage during this transitional period.

Although the league has not yet publicly revised its projections beyond 2027-2028, the consensus among those who understand the NHL's financial mechanics best leaves little room for doubt. The coming years could fundamentally redraw the economic balance of professional hockey in North America, and the teams that anticipate this shift most effectively will be the ones best positioned to capitalize on it.

title: Lionel Messi bids farewell to father who guided his glittering career
description: Argentina football icon Lionel Messi bid farewell Sunday to his father Jorge, the global star's emotional anchor and agent since childhood who passed away following a battle with cancer aged 68.Jorge left behind his job in Argentina, his wife, and his three other children to settle in Spain with Lionel.
fullText:
Argentina football icon Lionel Messi bid farewell Sunday to his father Jorge, the global star's emotional anchor and agent since childhood who passed away following a battle with cancer aged 68.

The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner touched down on a private flight from Miami late on Saturday with his wife Antonela Roccuzzo and their children.

A private ceremony with close family and a few Argentina teammates took place at a cemetery in the town of Perez, adjacent to Rosario, later Sunday.

The gates of the town's El Prado cemetery displayed handwritten messages from fans -- "Stay strong, Leo, we love you" and "Stay strong, Messi family" -- alongside a large floral wreath.

Messi's teammates rallied around their captain following the announcement that Jorge Messi had passed away late Friday at a clinic in Rosario.

"It will surely do him good for us to be there," Boca Juniors midfielder Leandro Paredes told journalists after his team's match on Saturday.

"I need to speak with a few of my teammates to see if we go now or sometime tomorrow."

According to media reports midfielder Rodrigo de Paul -- a close friend of Messi and his Inter Miami teammate -- travelled to Argentina.

After scoring a goal in a 2-1 defeat to Monterrey in Miami on Saturday, De Paul paid tribute by taking off his shirt to reveal Messi's number 10 jersey.

There was a handful of fans outside the cemetery, including 15-year-old Lucas Blanco, who hung a sign reading "Stay strong, Messi" on the gate.

"He has brought so much joy to this country, now it's our turn to give a little back and offer him some comfort," he said.

"We drove 700 kilometres to be here. We wanted to stand by Leo during this time," said Carlos and Ana, a couple who travelled from Tres Arroyos, a town south of Buenos Aires.

The cause of death was not disclosed, but local media reported that Jorge Messi had been suffering from cancer.

His unusual absence from the World Cup in June had already attracted attention.

Messi's family asked the media for "humanity" during the tournament amid persistent rumours over Jorge's health.

After bursting into tears after scoring against Algeria, 39-year-old Messi had admitted to dealing with "a situation outside of sports".

"I went through a few difficult, complicated days," he later acknowledged. "But I am grateful to the entire delegation and my teammates, because they stood by me, as always."

Immediately after the World Cup final defeat against Spain, Messi returned to spend a few days with his family in Rosario.

A guiding figure throughout his son's career, Jorge Messi was his first coach who left everything behind to accompany his son to Spain.

A metalworker in Rosario, 340 km north of Buenos Aires, Jorge managed youth teams at the small local club Grandoli.

He was the one who introduced Argentina's future captain to the game aged four on vacant lots where local kids played.

His life changed course in 2000 when Barcelona invited the young prodigy, then aged 13, to Catalonia to continue treatment for a growth hormone deficiency while playing for the club's youth teams.

Jorge left behind his job in Argentina, his wife, and his three other children to settle in Spain with Lionel.

"When we arrived in Barcelona, I used to lock myself in my room to cry alone, and my father did the same -- either without me seeing him or thinking I didn't see him. We pretended we were both fine, but we were struggling," Messi later said.

His father was later the agent who negotiated contracts on his behalf, from Barcelona to Paris Saint-Germain and Inter Miami.

Messages of sympathy have poured in since Saturday from the football world, including from the clubs Messi played for and the Spanish Football Federation.

The Argentine Football Association (AFA) ordered a minute's silence before matches and that black armbands be worn at games across all age groups for the week.

title: Bullpen shines on rainy day, as White Sox take key series from Guardians
description: The South Siders extended their lead over Cleveland to four games with Sunday’s victory
fullText:
Baseball feels more organic when Nancy Faust is in a booth with an organ. Her presence in the ballpark this afternoon, which precluded the usual barrage of pop songs, crowd-stimulating noises, and things that my dad would refer to as "canned bullshit," set the tone for what turned out to be an improbably fun day at the ballpark as the White Sox staked themselves a season-high four-game lead in the AL Central with a 5-2 win over the Guardians.

This is a Sox team that has made its hay with youthful energy. But even without the thumping bass that typically blasts from Rate Field's PA system, the action on the field and the feeling in the stands was as vibrant as ever. When it appeared that Cleveland would put a damper on the 30,000 strong crowd's supportive push with three straight hits and two runs against Davis Martin to open the game, the Sox responded with three consecutive hits of their own to start their part of the action.

The Sox only managed to get one run out of their hit parade, though. For a moment, when Guardians starter Joey Cantillo punched out three consecutive hitters to escape the early jam, it seemed as if the building momentum had been stifled.

One two-hour rain delay later, it felt like it didn't matter. When Tim Herrin took the ball for Cleveland in relief of Cantillo, it was a whole new ballgame. Herrin did his job, but his successor Craig Yoho couldn't. For the second straight day, the Guardians had grabbed themselves a 2-0 lead before falling victim to a big crooked number from the South Siders. After taking an inning to warm up, Miguel Vargas, Randal Grichuk and Braden Montgomery all reached base in succession with two outs before the other Montgomery broke things open with one swing of the bat.

For most of the last half-decade, the thought of 20,000 Sox fans waiting out a two-hour rain delay while trailing would have been nigh-unthinkable. The ones who stood tall through the pause were also rewarded by witnessing Hagen Smith's long-awaited big league debut. He lived up to every bit of the scouting report, throwing just 25 of 48 pitches for strikes (and even fewer in the zone) and walking four over two innings. He also struck out three, drew whiffs on 33% of the swings against him, and kept the opponent off the board long enough for the Sox offense to take control of the game.

That's not a location chart that's going to get it done long-term, but he got away with it today, which is hard to be mad about in a big league debut. Despite having all pitched just yesterday, Sean Newcomb, Bryan Hudson and Jordan Hicks once against answered the bell with aplomb, keeping Cleveland off the board for three more innings.

One critical piece of last night's bullpen picture was missing, as Grant Taylor was clearly unavailable, leaving Trevor Richards to handle the ninth inning. As Richards walked two of the first three hitters he saw in the ninth inning, flashbacks circulated of the righthander's two-for-one blown save(s) in Boston earlier this week.

Magnifying the unease was the man who stepped to the plate as the tying run as a wild pitch sent the baserunners to second and third.

They're playing Cleveland. You already know who it was.

Maybe this Sox team really is different. Perhaps the ghosts of Josh Naylor have been exorcised. Richards stiffened his back and got José Ramírez to fly out to Brenton Doyle in center field, allowing a meaningless run to cross over in the process. It subsequently took just a single pitch to get Rhys Hoskins to sail one straight into Braden Montgomery's glove, securing a 5-3 win for the good guys, and a four-game lead over both the Guardians and the Twins. Detroit now occupies second place alone at 58-60, 3 ½ games behind.

If the conclusion to this week's series in Boston felt like a missed opportunity to make a statement that this isn't a team that's going to go away down the stretch, I'd gauge that this weekend did well to compensate. The Sox offense has been touch-and-go as the league enters a sudden dead-ball era, the way the offense and pitching alternated picking up each other's slack over the course of these three games was encouraging in the big picture. Nobody's going to mistake the White Sox for a juggernaut, but with Smith and Tanner McDougal — who appeared ready to make his own debut had Richards not been able to work out of his own jam — providing real bullpen upside, I'd have a pretty big pit in my stomach if I was a rival AL Central team.

The Sox have a rest day at home tomorrow before welcoming the Cincinnati Reds for three games on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday. It would be prudent for them to use that rest day wisely, as this series also kicks off a stretch of 16 consecutive game days, a gauntlet that could very well decide the fate of the division.

The highly-anticipated Pope Hat giveaway set for Tuesday night has already sold out, and the thought of newly-minted ace Sean Burke toeing the rubber with 40,000 Catholics-for-a-night roaring behind them in pursuit of an extended division lead can't help but tickle the imagination. That'll be followed up on Wednesday with Luis Castillo's second turn through the rotation on the South Side, with Thursday's starter yet to be announced. The first two are set for 6:40 p.m. CT, while Thursday is a 1:10 matinee contest.

All of that extra attention certainly hasn't stopped the third-year megastar from piecing together one-of-a-kind performances as both a scorer and facilitator in recent weeks. Already ranked atop the entire WNBA in points per game created (40.0), Clark has turned things up a few notches higher since the All-Star break.

To put that into further perspective: Clark is far-and-away the No. 1 on this season's list, creating a sizable gap between herself and Alyssa Thomas (35.2) of the Phoenix Mercury.

In the league's history, no player has ever surpassed over 40 points generated per game.

It stands as just one of the many ways Caitlin Clark and her teammates have turned rewriting the league's history books into an almost night-for-night tradition.

As it stands, the Fever (20-12) are fourth in the WNBA standings, and a half-game ahead of both the Atlanta Dream and New York Liberty for the No. 1 spot in the Eastern Conference. "We take our bond serious. Me and (Caitlin), we like to think that our backcourt comes from love for one, and I think that I want to see her be great and vice versa. A lot of it is just love and energy, honestly."

For opposing title-contenders across the WNBA, figuring out ways to combat that record-setting backcourt will likely become topic No. 1 with the postseason set to begin next month.

title: Don Nelson, former NBA coach and 5-time champion as a player, dies at 86
description: Don Nelson was one of two coaches in NBA history to have at least 250 wins with three different franchises — Milwaukee, Dallas and Golden State.
fullText:
Don Nelson, the NBA's three-time Coach of the Year and a five-time champion, has died at the age of 86, his family said in a statement.

"On Sunday morning our beloved husband, dad, grandfather and great-grandfather Don Nelson peacefully went to be with the Lord, surrounded by his loving family," the statement said. "Throughout his last week, friends and family encircled him with love, sharing the blessing of his friendship and revisiting treasured memories."

As a player, Nelson played 11 of his 14 seasons with the Boston Celtics, winning five NBA championships before going on to coach after he retired from playing.

He last coached for the Golden State Warriors in 2010 and retired as the NBA's winningest coach. Over his 30-year career, he coached four teams, including the Milwaukee Bucks, New York Knicks and Dallas Mavericks.

Nelson also served as general manager for all three franchises and is one of two coaches in NBA history to have at least 250 wins with the three teams.

Dallas Mavericks Governor Patrick Dumont said Nelson helped transform the franchise and brought "a winning culture" to the city.

"Don Nelson was a true original whose impact on the Dallas Mavericks and the game of basketball will endure for generations ... His influence can be seen throughout Mavericks history and across the NBA today," Dumont said.

Nelson introduced what is now known as the point forward, and his up-tempo style of offense created a buzz. He said the idea of shifting from the dominant big men of the 1970s to an offense focused on speed and the fast break came from his playing days under Celtics Hall of Fame coach Red Auerbach.

"The league really hadn't seen an offense like the one we were running, and the results were undeniable," Nelson wrote in 2016 in The Players' Tribune.

Nelson was best known for his stint in Oakland, where he drafted Stephen Curry and was credited with helping build the Warriors' ascent.

"'Nellie' was one of the most innovative and influential coaches in NBA history and an iconic figure in Warriors history. He was a true basketball visionary who saw the game differently and was never afraid to challenge conventional thinking," the Warriors said in a statement posted to social media.

Nelson will be remembered for his authenticity, personality and passion for basketball, the organization said.

In a statement, Curry said, "The story is [Nelson] never liked rookies, but from Day 1, he challenged me and gave me an opportunity to be my best self on the court ... He had an immeasurable impact on the sport and will go down as one of the greatest minds in the history of the game."

"Don Nelson revolutionized NBA basketball through his fearlessness, ingenuity and deep conviction," NBA Commissioner Adam Silver said in a statement. "He brought an unmistakable personality to everything he did, and his impact on our sport will continue to be felt for generations."

The Celtics, in a statement, highlighted Nelson's playing career and said it would be a mistake to let his coaching career overshadow his gameplay.

In Game 7 of the 1969 NBA Finals against his former team, the Los Angeles Lakers, Nelson "converted one of the most famous shots in playoff history—a foul-line jumper which dropped through the basket after hitting the back rim and bouncing several feet straight up," the organization said.

"The Celtics extend our deep condolences to Nelson's family, loved ones, and everyone he touched through his rich and impactful life in basketball and beyond," the statement said. "The shot, taken with just over a minute to go in the game and the Celtics clinging to a 103-102 lead, was an essential play in helping secure Boston's 11th NBA title in 13 seasons."

Nelson won all five of his playing titles with the Celtics, and in 1978, two years after his final season as a player, his number 19 was raised to the rafters in Boston.

In 2000, Nelson revealed a prostate cancer diagnosis and later said he had his cancerous prostate removed, with doctors having found no sign that the disease had spread.

Nelson's cause of death wasn't revealed. He is survived by his children and his wife, Joy.

description: WASHINGTON — The Phoenix Mercury continued their tough road trip Sunday against the Washington Mystics, but had no answers as they fell 95-75, with their margin for error continuing to thin. fullText:
WASHINGTON — The Phoenix Mercury continued their tough road trip Sunday against the Washington Mystics, but had no answers as they fell 95-75, with their margin for error continuing to thin.

Phoenix and Washington began the matchup competitively, both trading runs in the first quarter and separated by a single point. However, that competitiveness vanished for the Mercury as the Mystics took charge the rest of the way with key shooting and tough defense that kept Phoenix from scoring more than 17 points in the second and third quarters.

Sixteen turnovers also turned into 18 points for Washington, highlighting Phoenix's inability to take care of the ball.

The Mercury's defense also had no answers for the Mystics' offense, allowing them to shoot 50% from the field and score 42 points in the paint.

What made the loss even more difficult was the early departure of Kelsey Plum, who left the game with left calf tightness. Plum was playing her fourth game with Phoenix since being acquired at the trade deadline, leaving the team without one of its dynamic shooters and playmakers.

Head coach Nate Tibbetts said the team wanted to play it safe, prioritizing Plum's health rather than pushing her.

The concern for Phoenix's playoff position is now more apparent than ever. With another three-game skid, the Mercury's chances for a postseason berth continue to slip away. The team's road trip has also made it difficult to find time to collect itself and practice, making it an even harder task for a group that has been trying to find consistency.

While Sunday's loss came against one of the hottest teams in the WNBA, going toe-to-toe with Washington for one quarter showcased what Phoenix could have done if it had maintained its rhythm. However, when Washington punched back, the Mercury never found a way to recover.

title: Marwan Rahiki predicts Noche UFC KO of Tommy McMillen to show he's 'superstar'
description: Marwan Rahiki thinks Tommy McMillen's record-setting UFC win just "means you don't have knockout power."
fullText:
Marwan Rahiki's friend urged him to take a swing and call out Tommy McMillen. Now he has the matchup scheduled for UFC Fight Night 288 next month.

The UFC will pit two of its most compelling featherweight prospects together at Noche UFC on Sept. 12 when Rahiki (9-0 MMA, 2-0 UFC) meets McMillen (11-0 MMA, 2-0 UFC) in a battle of undefeated fighters at Desert Diamond Arena in Glendale, Ariz. (Paramount+)

Some would argue this is a matchup that could've been held until further down the line, with higher stakes, but Rahiki is all about doing it now.

"I was surprised, but at the same time, I'm not that surprised," Rahiki told MMA Junkie. "The only thing that surprised me is putting undefeated against undefeated, but they just did this with Movsar Evloev and Lerone Murphy. Someone's got to go. Someone's got to go up. Someone's got to stay where they are, and I never say no to fights. The only thing is the time (to prepare). I came here (to Morocco) to spend time with family, but when the UFC calls, I can't say no. I love this.

"This is the most exciting fight I've ever had. The first time I heard the name, I was like, 'Wow.' So happy – I don't remember myself being so happy with a fight, with the opponent. I've always wanted to fight the best guys."

Although McMillen is getting a lot of attention currently for his polarizing personality, relationship with UFC contender Sean O'Malley and his in-cage performances so far, there's a lot that Rahiki brings to the table in his own right.

Rahiki, 24, is the younger man to McMillen, 28, and has finished all nine of his career victories to this point – including five in the first round.

"It's an entertaining fight, an entertaining style and someone who isn't just going to try to run away," Rahiki said. "I think it will be a great night for Noche UFC. I think it's just perfect. He wanted a Mexican, but I think this is even better. I hope he goes and watches some Moroccan fighters and has an idea of what's coming."

McMillen requested to fight at Noche UFC off the back of his record-setting performance at UFC Fight Night 281 in July. He set a new three-round UFC record for significant strikes landed in his third-round TKO of Alberto Montes, and with that came plenty of shine.

Rahiki has a different perspective around that record, however, and is emphatic in his ability to prevent that type of striking pressure.

"When someone breaks a significant strikes record – as I see it – (just) finish the fight in the first round," Rahiki said. "I don't care about significants. I never think, 'I'm going to land the more significant strikes.' That means you don't have knockout power. That means it takes you that long. It doesn't take me that long to finish, and that's the goal this fight: Go in there to knock him out in the first round. Go in there to knock him out. If he comes forward, it will be done quick. If he stays smart, he might survive a couple of minutes. But the result will be the same.

"I am very excited about it. I hope there will be a press conference so we can see (if he's trash talk). I want that energy. That's why I'm excited. That's a guy, like a superstar, and I feel like I'm a superstar, too. But my division is different than his vision, I believe. I want to be champion. I want to be a respected champion. ... I don't want to be the villain. I have a lot of fans, a lot of great fans."

title: Ancient Roman shipwreck discovered off Sicily coast
description: Italy's culture minister says it is one of the most important underwater archaeological finds in years.
fullText:
Italian divers have discovered an ancient Roman shipwreck off the coast of Sicily, believed to be more than 2,000 years old.

The vessel was found piled high with hundreds of well-preserved containers, which were used to transport goods such as wine and olive oil.

Italy's Culture Minister Alessandro Giuli hailed the wreck as "one of the most important underwater archaeological discoveries of recent years".

Specialist police divers found the ship around 46m (150ft) deep, after a tip-off from fishermen. The wreckage is 21m (69ft) long and 6m (20ft) wide, according to reports in local media.

The culture ministry says it dates from the second or 1st Century BC.

Fisherman and free-diver Giacomo De Mola described stumbling across the historic vessel while surveying the seabed near Mazara del Vallo.

He wrote on social media that he had decided to dive and investigate after seeing something that appeared to be a large rock on his scanner.

"I get closer. And my heart stops. It wasn't a rock," he said. Instead, he saw hundreds of amphorae - tall ceramic jars used to store goods in the ancient era, mostly wine, oil or grain.

"This is, without a doubt, the most incredible discovery of my life," he said. "It's hard to describe what it feels like to be among the first humans, in nearly 20 centuries, to see that place again."

He posted a video of the wreck, showing eels, snappers and "countless marine life" living among the jars, noting: "The sea never ceases to amaze us.

"This time we didn't just find a wreck, we found a piece of our history."

Specialist divers from the cultural heritage protection arm of Italy's police, known as the Carabinieri Art Squad, were sent to the site.

Officials say safety measures will be taken to safeguard it while it undergoes investigation, as experts work to determine the nature of the wreck and learn more about its cargo.

The Mediterranean seabed is thought to be scattered with similar ancient wrecks.

Another 1st or 2nd Century BC vessel was found north-west of Rome in 2023, again laden with hundreds of amphorae.

In 2018, a Greek merchant ship dating back more than 2,400 years was found lying on its side off the Bulgarian coast. At the time, it was hailed as the world's oldest-known intact shipwreck.

title: Discord-delete – Delete all your Discord messages from your data export
description: Bulk-delete your Discord messages and reactions from your data package - DatCodeMania/discord-delete
fullText:
Bulk-delete your Discord messages and reactions, driven by your GDPR data package.

discord-delete reads the exact channel and message IDs from your data package so it only sends DELETEs. The search API is never touched, and nothing breaks on a UI change. It removes messages and reactions, headless or through an interactive terminal UI (TUI).

Try discord-delete using a demo package. It's fake data so no token/account is needed and nothing is deleted.

Automating a user account is against Discord's Terms of Service and can get it banned. While this tool cooperates with Discord's rate limits, that doesn't fully protect against a ban.

AUR pushes are currently disabled. It is suggested to install using an alternate method.

Any AUR helper for discord-delete-bin:

dnf (Fedora, RHEL, Rocky, Alma)

Swap amd64 for arm64 on ARM. Alpine .apk in releases.

Download the official binaries from the releases page.

The binaries are not code-signed. On macOS, a manually downloaded binary may be blocked by Gatekeeper on first run: choose Open from the right-click menu, or run xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine ./discord-delete (Homebrew does this for you). On Windows, SmartScreen may warn: click More info, then Run anyway.

Obtain your data package: in Discord, go to Settings > Data & Privacy > Request Data and enable both Messages and Activity (Activity for reactions). Discord emails it within a few hours to days.

Then point discord-delete at your package:

During a run: space or p pauses and resumes, [ and ] nudge the pacing floor slower or faster by 0.2s per step, q quits.

Full help: discord-delete --help

Deleting messages across a large account takes days. Older messages hit a shared, account-wide limit that caps deletion at roughly one every two seconds, so my own 400,000+ message account, the largest tested so far, took over a week. discord-delete can be run headless on a server without any babysitting. Configure a ntfy topic (--ntfy) to receive:

ntfy.sh topics are publicly viewable by default. Notifications carry only counts and status, no message content or channel names. Anyone who can read your topic can pause/stop the run, so use a hard-to-guess topic, or your own ntfy server.

Every run (including dry) writes a plain-text report when it ends: finished, stopped with q, or aborted.

It holds the run's mode and status, how long it took, and per phase how many items were deleted, skipped, failed, and how many were already gone from an earlier run. Then it lists everything Discord refused to delete (403), grouped by server, with Discord's own reason and whether you are still a member.

Missing Access means you lost access to that server or DM, so rejoin or reopen it and run again: a re-run retries what was skipped and skips what is already deleted.

System messages: Your package includes the ones you triggered (starting a call, renaming a group, adding or removing someone), and these are not deletable. They look like normal messages until Discord rejects the delete.

Reports land in your OS cache directory, timestamped, next to the resume log:

Use --report PATH to write it somewhere specific, or DISCORD_DELETE_STATE_DIR to move the whole directory.

When a run completes, that path is printed with a button. Click it or press o to open the report. The path is also directly ctrl-clickable (cmd on macOS) in some terminals which support OSC 8 hyperlinks.

That directory also holds the resume log, <key>.deleted.log, one confirmed-gone ID per line. It is keyed by account and therefore works across packages. Delete the log to start over from scratch.

The TUI also saves its settings to <key>.config.json in that directory, so the next run for that account starts where you left off. The token is not saved here. Any explicit flag overrides a saved value, and headless runs ignore the file.

discord-delete also removes reactions you added, reading them from the Activity data in your package. They run as a separate phase, set up in the TUI like everything else.

Headless, enable them with --reactions (messages first by default), or run them on their own:

Your data package holds the exact channel and message IDs for everything you posted, so discord-delete never has to search. It sends one DELETE per item to Discord's REST API, the same endpoint the client uses, and reads the response to decide what to do next.

Discord's rate-limit buckets are per channel, so each channel is cleared serially at roughly human pace, many in parallel. Older messages share one account-wide bucket, so the run reduces to one worker. Pacing is adaptive per channel (AIMD off a floor), so a run settles on the fastest rate Discord tolerates. A 429 only means slow down: it pauses every worker without aborting. Only a sustained wall of 401s (which is probably a dead token) aborts.

Every confirmed-gone ID (deleted or already absent) is written to a log as it happens. A re-run filters those out before queuing anything, so a crash or exit loses no progress.

Deleting needs your user token (a dry run does not). Two ways to provide it:

On Linux, a snap or Flatpak browser is used only if nothing else is installed. Those builds run with a private /tmp and cannot read the throwaway profile, so browser sign-in may fail with them.

The token is then verified against Discord (GET /users/@me), and the tool shows who you are logged in as.

The two most popular alternatives are below, both browser-based. A large account takes days on any of these; discord-delete is the one you start in a console and leave alone. Discrub is the closest comparison: actively maintained, with a well-designed web app for anyone not comfortable in a terminal. Pick whichever suits your use case.

The attack affected the communication operations of the fire and police departments, including the routing of 911 calls.

Suisun City officials said in a statement that the attack posed no imminent threat to the public and that all public safety services remain active. The computer network was shut down to contain the threat and preserve evidence for a federal investigation.

Suisun City dispatchers are taking emergency police and fire calls through the Solano County dispatch center. Online city services and internal operations remained temporarily unavailable as of Sunday morning while cybersecurity experts investigate the incident and work to restore systems.

The attack is believed to be the first of its kind in the city of 30,000 located 55 miles north of San Francisco, as the threat of cybersecurity disruptions of essential services in local communities across the country grows.

Going after internet technologies that control communications in public safety agencies would be a new frontier for cyberattackers that federal agencies believe could be affiliated with Iran.

Federal agencies are investigating cyberattacks targeting municipal water systems in a dozen states. Late last month, the FBI, the Environmental Protection Agency and the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency all warned that cyberattackers remotely accessed online infrastructure for water and wastewater systems in at least seven states.

The agencies warned that Iran-affiliated hackers were targeting internet-connected industrial controllers “to cause disruptive effects within the United States.”

Water systems in smaller communities depend on internet-connected automated systems, with many lacking the resources to provide adequate security. In response to the attacks, a bipartisan group of lawmakers last week urged the restoration of federal funding for Department of Homeland Security programs designed to coordinate multi-state cybersecurity efforts.

Gov. Gavin Newsom’s office, in a statement to The Times, said that there is no evidence that California water systems were among those targeted in the recent spate of attacks. fullText:
The Japanese Patent Office has declared one of Red’s key Raw video patents as invalid, following a challenge by Panasonic.

The court determined that many of the claims made in the patent, first filed in the US in 2008, would have been obvious to someone skilled in the subject area and familiar with existing developments.

The news, first reported by Thom Hogan, put Nikon’s video subsidiary in the position of trying to defend a patent that Nikon had previously argued was invalid.

The patent itself describes a high-resolution video camera that compresses its Raw data, and appears to correspond to the patent at the center of historic claims against Sony and Apple and the almost inevitable counter-suits from those companies. We reported on many of these challenges, as well as Nikon’s, over the years.

Nikon famously resolved the dispute by buying the company. Some of Red’s cinema camera and Raw knowledge has subsequently been applied to recent Nikon models.

It’s difficult to know what the impact the rejection of this patent will be, given Canon, Panasonic, Sony and Blackmagic Design all now produce cameras with internal Raw video capture. One possibility the abolition of the license fees reportedly due to Red from users of Apple’s ProRes RAW codec. But given Red went from being privately held to being absorbed into Nikon, it’s difficult to get a sense for how significant these might be. And, of course, we shouldn’t assume even a minor cost reduction would necessarily get passed on to consumers.

Let’s start with the powertrain. Drivers supervising the car as it makes its way down the highway will have plenty of time to get comfortable, thanks to the new Buick’s CATL-supplied 80.6 kWh lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery, reportedly good for up to 702 km (~436 miles) of range on the Chinese cycle.
